designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Very print-friendly: one solid ink with no halftones, brush strokes heavy enough to hold on a 156-mesh screen and to survive a white underbase on the black tee, and plenty of open space so the ink won't pile up. The serif title and italic captions are big enough to stay sharp. From 3 m it reads as a tidy grid, and the joke (four 'Turn around.' steps, then 'Sigh.') works up close. Weak spots: the turn sequence doesn't read as a steady spin. Step 3 looks like a dog just standing, and in step 2 the front legs get tangled. The thinnest marks (motion ticks, sniff marks in step 1, the sigh ticks, eyelash strokes) are the first places the ink could fill in or break up on the black tee. The whole print is a bit small and narrow on the back.
designs.fix: Redraw steps 2 to 5 so the dog turns visibly further in each one (side view, three-quarter view, tail chasing, curled spin) and fix the leg tangle in step 2. In the same pass, thicken the hairline motion ticks to at least 1 pt at print size.
